newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's MPLA changes mind over Savimbi offer.
newsitem.headline: Angola's MPLA changes mind over Savimbi offer.

text.p: Leaders of Angola's ruling MPLA want the party to withdraw its offer to make former rebel UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi the country's vice president, sparking new fears over the country's peace process.

The Political Bureau, the MPLA's top decision-making body, said in a statement Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos should withdraw his offer because UNITA would not let Savimbi take up the post.

Dos Santos created the vice presidency as a reconciliatory gesture aimed at giving the former guerrillas "special status" in a unity government, but a UNITA congress last week rebuffed it, saying Savimbi needed to focus on transforming his organisation into a political party.

A government of national unity is meant to be part of a peace deal that followed two decades of civil war on independence from Portugal in 1975, but delays in demobilising former fighters have hampered the peace process.

"The congress of UNITA categorically rejected the nomination of its president for the vice-presidency and the Political Bureau understands this to mean that the compromise relative to the guarantee of 'special status' is then halted," said the MPLA statement broadcast on state radio on Wednesday night.
"It insists that the government delegation in the joint commission declare the clause invalid."
The Angolan government and UNITA agreed to end two decades of civil war after year-long negotiations that led to the signing of the Lusaka Protocol peace pact in November 1994.
The Political Bureau said the post for Savimbi had been created in the spirit of national reconciliation, and slammed UNITA's public rejection of it months later as disrespectful.

"UNITA took six months to respond to the invitation of President dos Santos to assume one of the two vice-presidency posts and made it public, instead of following the formal channels which shows a lack of respect for the sovereign organs," the statement said.
The MPLA also accused UNITA of dragging its feet over disarming troops and handing in heavy weaponry.
UNITA in turn accuses the government of failing in its obligations under terms of the peace accord. It says soldiers had not been confined to barracks and foreign mercenaries had not been expelled.
On Thursday the United Nations' special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, travelled to UNITA's headquarters in Bailundo for the second time in a week for talks with Savimbi.
Beye, who met dos Santos earlier in the week, has expressed concern that there has been no progress in the peace process for two months.
The U.N. peacekeeping force is expected to withdraw its soldiers as scheduled next February.
